title: Computer Won't Turn On
cardText: Diagnose a desktop or laptop that does not respond when attempting to start.
Check power delivery, cables, chargers, batteries, power supply components and internal connections.
Identify likely power faults before replacing hardware.
text: This guide covers desktop and laptop computers with no apparent power or startup response.
Begin by checking external power delivery before investigating internal components.
Follow the relevant desktop or laptop troubleshooting branch.
If the computer powers on but produces no display, use the Computer Turns On But No Display guide.
Do not open power supplies, damaged chargers or sealed batteries.

checkPowerSource.title: Check power delivery
body: Test the wall outlet with another known-working device.
If using a power board, surge protector or extension lead, bypass it and test directly from a working wall outlet.
Look for damaged plugs, overheating or signs of electrical failure.
If the computer still receives no power from a known-working source, continue checking its power cable or charger.

restorePower.title: External power fault identified
body: The outlet, power board or extension lead is not supplying reliable power.
Use a known-working outlet and replace any faulty power board or extension lead.
If a breaker repeatedly trips or the outlet shows signs of damage, arrange an electrician.
Retest the computer after restoring reliable power.

checkPowerCable.title: Check power cable or charger
body: Inspect the power cable, charger and connectors for damage.
Check for frayed insulation, bent pins, loose plugs or signs of overheating.
For desktops, try another compatible mains power cable where available.
For laptops, verify that the charger connector fits securely and is compatible with the computer.
Stop using damaged cables or adapters.

replacePowerCable.title: Replace damaged cable or charger
body: A damaged power cable or charger may prevent the computer from receiving power.
Replace the faulty component with a compatible, correctly rated replacement.
For USB-C charging, ensure the charger and cable meet the laptop's power requirements.
Retest the computer after replacement.

desktopOrLaptop.title: Identify computer type
body: Select the type of computer being diagnosed.
Desktop and laptop computers use different power arrangements and require different diagnostic procedures.
For all-in-one computers, follow the manufacturer's power supply instructions.

checkPsuSwitch.title: Check desktop power supply
body: Inspect the rear of the computer where the mains cable connects.
Some desktop power supplies have an I/O rocker switch that can become accidentally switched off.
If a switch is fitted, I indicates On and O indicates Off.
Check for physical damage or signs of overheating around the power supply.
Do not adjust any voltage selector switch or open the PSU casing.
If the PSU switch was off, correct it and retest.

link.name: ASUS: Motherboard power troubleshooting
link.description: Official guidance for checking desktop power supplies and motherboard power connections.

checkPsuSwitch.alt: Rear of a desktop power supply showing the I and O rocker switch beside the mains inlet
checkPsuSwitch.caption: Some desktop power supplies have a separate I/O switch beside the mains connector.

enablePsu.title: Power supply switch issue
body: The desktop PSU switch was set to Off.
Set the switch to I and test the computer.
If the system remains unresponsive, continue checking the internal power connections.

checkMotherboardPowerConnectors.title: Check motherboard power connections
body: This step applies to desktop computers with accessible internal components.
Disconnect mains power and follow appropriate anti-static precautions before opening the case.
Inspect the main 24-pin ATX motherboard power connector.
Check the CPU power connector, usually a 4-pin or 8-pin connection near the processor.
Ensure the connectors are fully seated and their retaining clips are secure.
Check for signs of burnt, damaged or loose connectors.
Use the correct power supply cables and never force incompatible connectors.
Do not open the power supply itself.

link.name: ASUS: Motherboard power connections
link.description: Manufacturer troubleshooting for ATX and CPU power connections.

checkMotherboardPowerConnectors.alt: Motherboard showing the main ATX and CPU power connector locations
checkMotherboardPowerConnectors.caption: Check that the motherboard ATX and CPU power connectors are securely seated.

reconnectMotherboardPower.title: Reconnect motherboard power
body: A motherboard or CPU power connector was loose.
With mains power disconnected, reconnect the correct cable until its retaining clip is secure.
Inspect the connector for damage or overheating.
Reassemble the computer and retest.
If the computer still fails, continue with further power supply diagnostics.

checkMotherboardLed.title: Check motherboard standby power
body: Some motherboards have a standby-power LED that indicates part of the board is receiving power.
Check the motherboard manual to identify whether this indicator exists.
A lit standby LED suggests some power is reaching the motherboard but does not prove that the power supply is fully functional.
An unlit or absent indicator does not automatically mean the power supply has failed.
Use this observation alongside the other power checks.

testPowerButton.title: Check desktop power switch wiring
body: Inspect the case power button for physical damage or a sticking mechanism.
With mains power disconnected, check the front-panel power-switch cable where it connects to the motherboard.
Confirm the connector is attached to the correct header pins using the motherboard manual.
Look for disconnected, damaged or loose wiring.
Do not short motherboard pins unless following an approved service procedure.
If the button and wiring are intact, continue investigating the power supply.

repairPowerButton.title: Repair desktop power switch
body: The case power switch or its front-panel wiring may be faulty.
Disconnect mains power before adjusting any connectors.
Use the motherboard manual to identify the correct power-switch header pins.
Reconnect loose wiring or replace the faulty switch assembly.
Reassemble and retest the computer.
If the fault remains, investigate the power supply and motherboard.

psuFailure.title: Test the desktop power supply
body: The desktop still does not start after checking external power and motherboard connections.
A faulty PSU is possible, but the motherboard or another component may also prevent startup.
Test with a known-working, electrically compatible PSU where available.
Only use the modular cables supplied with the replacement PSU. Cables from different PSU models are not necessarily interchangeable.
A standby LED or spinning fan does not prove that all PSU outputs are correct.
Never open a PSU casing because dangerous electrical charge can remain inside.
If a replacement PSU is unavailable, arrange further hardware testing.

link.name: ASUS: No-power hardware diagnostics
link.description: Official troubleshooting steps for power supplies and internal computer power faults.

replacePsu.title: Desktop PSU fault likely
body: The computer starts correctly with a known-working replacement power supply.
This strongly suggests that the original PSU or its associated cables were faulty.
Replace it with a compatible unit of sufficient capacity.
Use the cables supplied for the replacement PSU.
Test the computer after installation.

checkLaptopBattery.title: Check laptop charging indicators
body: Connect a compatible charger directly to a known-working outlet.
Check whether the laptop recognises the charger or displays a charging indicator.
If the battery may be completely discharged, allow approximately 15 to 30 minutes of charging.
Inspect the charging connector for physical damage or looseness.
Some laptops do not have a dedicated charging LED, so the absence of an indicator alone does not establish a fault.
Continue with the charger and power-reset checks as appropriate.

link.name: Dell: Laptop power troubleshooting
link.description: Official instructions for checking laptop adapters, charging and startup faults.

checkLaptopCharger.title: Test laptop charger
body: Inspect the charger and power cable for damage or overheating.
Check the charger's output voltage, power rating and connector compatibility.
For USB-C charging, confirm that the port supports charging and the adapter provides sufficient USB Power Delivery.
Try a known-working compatible charger if available.
Check for damage or looseness in the laptop's charging port.
If charging activity returns, continue with the laptop power reset.
If the laptop remains unresponsive with a compatible charger, an internal power fault is possible.

link.name: Dell: Troubleshoot laptop power problems
link.description: Manufacturer guidance for testing AC adapters and laptop power delivery.

laptopPowerReset.title: Perform laptop power reset
body: Disconnect the charger and unnecessary external devices.
If the laptop has an externally removable battery, remove it according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Hold the power button for approximately 15 to 20 seconds to discharge residual power.
Reconnect the removable battery if applicable, then reconnect the charger.
Test whether the laptop starts.
Some models use a dedicated reset button or manufacturer-specific reset procedure.
Do not dismantle a sealed laptop to disconnect its internal battery.

link.name: Dell: Troubleshoot laptop no-power problems
link.description: Manufacturer instructions for performing a laptop hard reset and checking power delivery.

powerResetFixed.title: Laptop power restored
body: The laptop started after the power reset.
Reconnect external devices one at a time.
Check that the battery charges and the laptop starts normally.
If the problem returns, investigate the charging circuit, battery or firmware.

testLaptopWithoutBattery.title: Test laptop without removable battery
body: Only perform this test if the laptop has an externally removable battery and the manufacturer supports operation using the charger alone.
Disconnect the charger before removing the battery.
Remove the battery following the manufacturer's procedure.
Reconnect the compatible charger and attempt to start the laptop.
Do not open a laptop with a sealed internal battery for this test.
If the battery is swollen or damaged, stop using the laptop and arrange professional service.
If the battery cannot be removed safely, proceed to further power diagnostics.

laptopBatteryFault.title: Laptop battery fault possible
body: The laptop starts when running from the charger without its removable battery.
The battery or its associated connection may be faulty.
Check the manufacturer's battery diagnostics.
Replace the battery only with a compatible, approved replacement.
Never reuse a swollen or physically damaged battery.

laptopPowerFault.title: Laptop internal power fault possible
body: The laptop remains unresponsive after testing the charger and performing a power reset.
Possible causes include the charging port, battery, internal charging circuit or motherboard.
Check for manufacturer-specific diagnostic light patterns.
Stop attempting to power on the laptop if it has liquid damage, signs of overheating or a swollen battery.
Record the laptop model, charger specifications and troubleshooting results.
Arrange further hardware diagnosis before replacing internal components.

link.name: Dell: Advanced laptop power diagnostics
link.description: Official troubleshooting for laptops that remain unresponsive after basic power checks.

motherboardFailure.title: Further desktop hardware diagnostics required
body: The desktop remains unresponsive after checking external power, internal connectors, the power switch and the PSU.
Possible causes include a motherboard fault, damaged power connector or internal electrical short.
Disconnect unnecessary peripherals and investigate recently installed hardware where appropriate.
Use known-working compatible components to isolate the fault.
Do not assume the motherboard has failed until the power supply and basic connections have been properly tested.
Arrange further hardware diagnostics or repair.

link.name: ASUS: Motherboard power troubleshooting
link.description: Official procedures for checking power delivery and diagnosing startup faults.
